rules: ONE in-progress at a time. Evidence before pass. Cross-contract features carry BOTH sides' proof in one entry (docs/spec/init-monorepo-contract/04-harness-binding.md). A design-tier entry may not go in-progress before its docs/design/ doc is approved (docs/spec/init-harness/06-design-first.md). New entries MAY carry an optional acceptance array (AC ids/text); when present, evidence names which AC each command proved (docs/spec/init-harness/02-artifacts-and-templates.md 2.2) — entries below predate it and were recorded as-built, so they have none. pass is terminal here; release readiness lives in docs/spec/init-release.

Return body {lateFee?, damageFee?, depositRefund?, note?} (ints ≥0) → payment rows via PaymentRecorderPort/Adapter writing the payments-owned TABLE directly (payments context is schema-only; same boundary trick as DressLookupAdapter; one transaction per settlement; zero/omitted amounts NOT recorded; the note rides on every row). features.title: Business outcomes survive the HTTP boundary: outcome bodies + error envelope across BE, contract, apps/fe and apps/qr-admin (ADR 0001; closes BE gap #6 + FE gap #8)

BE: libs/exceptions gains BusinessOutcomeException + ErrorDetail + ApiErrorResponseDto; the global filter renders the two shapes only; 9 command controllers map each returned domain error to its own snake_case code with a typed payload (dressIds / currentStatus / dressCode) and declare @ApiResponse 422 with a per-slice outcome DTO. AC3: the EXCLUDE race is translated by rental.repository -> RentalItemsOverlapError and converted in create-rental.service back to the SAME rejected_dress_unavailable outcome (re-queried dressIds). AC4: login/refresh reject as outcomes so 401 means only 'guard rejected the access token'. Contract re-emitted, both clients regenerated (idempotent re-run verified by md5). FE: src/api/errors.ts is now the single mapApiError seam (outcome vs fault); the three features/*/lib/is-conflict-error.ts files are deleted; dresses/rentals/today/auth render one designed state per code with new vi+en keys (parity checked by pnpm --filter fe arch). qr-admin: src/api/errors.ts replaces error-message.ts. After committing the regenerated layer, contract:check, the arch freshness item and a full `bash init.sh` are green. Real-browser runtime proof: `pnpm --filter fe e2e` (vi happy path vs migrated+seeded Postgres, BE :3000, Vite :5173) passes — sign-in, create-dress, booking, pickup, return-and-settle and the payments dialog all work on the new wire shapes; its board locators were scoped to the run's own rows so a non-empty database no longer breaks it.

AC2: every technical fault returns { error: { code, message, details?, correlationId } }; ValidationPipe 400s carry details[] per field

features.title: Auto-computed late fee at return, with owner-only waiver (FR-RENT-09)
features.evidence: 2026-08-09: design gate — use-case spec drafted at docs/design/rentals/settle-late-fee.md + contract check on the draft shape (2 blockers, 2 major, 2 minor); held at todo because the fee formula and waiver authority are business rules the lane forbids inventing. 2026-08-10: the shop owner answered (spec §6) — 200,000 VND per dress per day flat, no grace, no cap; the cleaning buffer does NOT count as late; only owner may charge less and must give a reason; the meaning change of `lateFee` accepted in place. Spec flipped to approved, then implemented and re-synced to as-built (§7). AC1: the rule is a pure value object (domain/late-fee.value-object.ts, 8 unit tests incl. buffer-irrelevance and month boundaries) reached through RentalEntity.lateFeeQuote; reference day is shopToday() in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh so money never depends on the VPS clock. features.title: The return dialog states the money: standard deposit out to the client, refund pre-filled, every amount read back grouped
features.evidence: UI/UX review finding P0: the return dialog asked staff to type a seven-digit refund from memory while the customer waited, with no thousand separators and no arithmetic on screen — the only screen in the app that moves real cash. AC1: `RentalDressDto` gained `depositAmount` (BE `DressSnapshot` + `DressLookupAdapter` now select `deposit_amount`; both read projections pass it through), documented in the DTO as the catalog STANDARD deposit and explicitly NOT what was collected — no deposit is recorded at booking time. Contract re-emitted and both clients regenerated in this commit. AC2: opening the dialog pre-fills `depositRefund` with `depositTotal − suggestedLateFee` (5.000.000 − 1.200.000 = 3.800.000 proven by a 2-dress vitest case; 3.000.000 in full when on time). AC3: a live reference block states `Cọc chuẩn N váy: X` and `Trừ phí F → hoàn lại khách Y`, recomputing as fees are typed (damage fee 500.000 → 2.500.000) and adding `Bạn đang nhập …` when the field disagrees with that arithmetic. AC4: each amount field renders its digits back grouped through `FormDescription`, which the shadcn form primitives already wire into `aria-describedby`. Gates: be 95 unit (today-board projection spec now asserts the deposit rides along per dress), fe 59 (+2 new cases, 1 rewritten for the pre-fill), qr-admin 13, root check/lint green, both builds green; `pnpm arch` freshness item red until this commit lands the generated layer, as designed. Assumption recorded for the shop owner: pre-filling `deposit − fees` encodes the deduction convention observed in `apps/be/scripts/smoke.sh` (lateFee 200.000 + refund 2.800.000 on a 3.000.000 deposit) and in the Playwright happy path; the field stays editable and the arithmetic is on screen, but the convention itself was never approved in writing the way the late-fee rules were.
acceptance: AC1: the standard deposit of each dress reaches the board and list reads, labelled as a reference rather than as a recorded fact
AC2: opening the return dialog pre-fills the refund with the standard deposit minus the suggested late fee, and the field stays editable
AC3: a live block shows deposit, fees deducted and the resulting refund, and says so when the typed refund differs
AC4: every amount field reads its own digits back with thousand separators, associated with the input for assistive tech

features.title: The new-rental form answers 'which dress is the problem' — per-dress availability before submit, and the rejection points at the named dresses
features.evidence: UI/UX review findings #4 and #5: `rejected_dress_unavailable` carries `dressIds` by design (ADR 0001 §3) and the form threw the payload away, leaving one sentence about 'some dress' for staff to resolve by removing dresses one at a time; and the picker searched the catalog with no idea of the dates already typed above it. FE-only — no API changed. AC1: each SELECTED dress now runs `GET /dresses/:id/availability` for the form's range (own child component per row, so the hook count stays static), rendering a `Còn trống` / `Vướng lịch` badge plus `Váy này bận tới hết <blockedUntilDate>` — the cleaning-buffer date, which is exactly the case staff cannot deduce; proven by a vitest case whose seeded booking ENDS before the asked range and still blocks it through the buffer. AC2: search results are deliberately NOT checked — one query per keystroke per row for an answer nobody asked for; recorded in the component. AC3: on rejection the form reads `dressIds` through a shape-checking helper and marks only those rows (destructive tint + per-row reason); proven with 2 dresses where only the second is refused — exactly one flag, and it sits in that row's `<li>`. All three dress rejections (`unavailable` / `retired` / `notFound`) get their own row copy. AC4: the flag is dropped as soon as the selection or either date changes, since it answered for the old range — proven by a case that changes the start date and watches the flag disappear. Gates: fe 63 tests (+4 new), check/lint/arch green, be untouched (95), qr-admin 13.
acceptance: AC1: a dress that cannot serve the typed date range says so in its row, with the date it is busy until, before anything is submitted
AC2: the availability check covers chosen dresses only, never the search results
AC3: a rejection marks exactly the dresses the server named, each with the reason for that code
AC4: a rejection is cleared as soon as the dates or the selection change

features.title: Dress photos appear where staff choose dresses — catalog list and the rental picker
features.evidence: UI/UX review finding #6: a dress shop recognises stock by sight, and `photoUrls` (shipped with catalog/manage-dress) was visible only on the detail page — the catalog list and the picker where dresses are actually CHOSEN were text-only. FE-only, no API change: the list DTO already carries the links. AC1: new kernel component `components/media/photo-thumbnail.tsx` renders the first photo at row size or a neutral icon; it is decorative (`alt=""`) because the dress code sits next to it in every caller, so announcing it again is noise. AC2: a dead link degrades to the placeholder instead of a broken-image glyph — the links are staff-pasted third-party URLs, so that is an ordinary state; the failed URL is remembered rather than a boolean flag, so a row that later receives a different photo tries again. AC3: wired into the catalog table (leading column, `sr-only` header) and into BOTH picker lists (search results and the chosen dresses, the latter through a new optional `photoUrl` on `SelectedDress`). Gates: fe 64 tests (+1 asserting the img src for a dress with a photo and its absence for one without — asserted on the DOM, since a decorative image has no `img` role), check/lint/arch green.

AC2: a broken photo link renders the placeholder, never a broken image

features.title: The morning board behaves like a tablet screen: it steps days without blanking, its actions are thumb-sized and per-row, and destructive confirms are the app's own
features.evidence: UI/UX review findings #7–#11, FE-only. AC1 (#7): the board date now moves inside `useTransition`, so a new day keeps the current board on screen at 50% opacity instead of dropping the whole route to the Suspense spinner — this screen is opened dozens of times a day and blanking it read as a reload. AC2 (#8): ± day buttons and a `Hôm nay` button, disabled when already there; `shiftDateIso` builds the neighbouring day through the local Date constructor, never `Date.parse` (which reads a bare yyyy-mm-dd as UTC and would step a day short east of Greenwich). Its test asserts the date INPUT after returning to today, because that board is already cached — no request is made, which is the point. AC3 (#9): the two board actions are `h-11` (44px) instead of the 32px `sm` used for secondary actions; they are pressed with a thumb while the other hand holds a dress. AC4 (#10): one mutation object serves every row, so `isPending` greyed out the entire list with no clue which hand-out was in flight — the spinner now marks the row whose id is in `variables`, while all buttons stay disabled to stop a double action. AC5 (#18): both board actions carry the customer in their accessible name, and the visible label is a prefix of it (WCAG 2.5.3); the vitest queries moved to regex names because the accessible name genuinely changed. AC6 (#11): `window.confirm` is gone from both destructive actions — new `ui/alert-dialog` primitive + a `ConfirmDialog` wrapper. The native dialog was wrong on a shop tablet for three reasons now recorded in the component: its buttons follow the OS language rather than the app's Vietnamese, it blocks the JS thread, and inside an installed PWA it renders as browser chrome that reads as a malfunction. The dismiss button says `Quay lại` rather than `Hủy`, because on the rentals list the CONFIRMED action is itself a cancel and two buttons reading Huỷ/Hủy side by side is a coin toss. Gates: fe 66 tests (+2 new, 3 rewritten to drive the real dialog), be 95, qr-admin 13, check/lint/arch/builds green, and `pnpm --filter fe e2e` passes against the real stack (1 passed, 15.9s) — the happy path clicks both resized board buttons.
acceptance: AC1: changing the board date keeps the previous board visible instead of blanking the route
AC2: the board steps one day at a time and returns to today in one tap
AC3: the two board actions meet the 44px touch target
AC4: only the row whose action is in flight shows a spinner, and no second action can start meanwhile
AC5: repeated board actions are distinguishable by accessible name
AC6: cancelling a rental and retiring a dress confirm through the app's own dialog, in Vietnamese, with a confirm button that states the action

features.title: Money COLLECTED is written down: deposit and rental fee recorded on an open rental, and the return dialog refunds what was actually taken (FR-PAY-02)
features.evidence: Design-tier, spec-before-code through docs/spec/init-feature-spec → docs/design/payments/record-collection.md, written at `draft` with the business rules as BLOCKER questions; the shop owner answered four (§6): a standalone action usable any time, amounts pre-filled from the catalog standard + the agreed price but editable, fees ARE deducted from the deposit, and rental fee is in scope alongside the deposit. Only then code. The payments context grew its first aggregate + command, which is exactly the trigger its own design doc had predicted. AC1 (unit + e2e): `POST /rentals/:rentalId/payments/collect` writes 1..2 rows in ONE transaction with the note on each, and any staff may do it (`payment:collect`) because the person holding the cash is the one at the counter. AC2 is the one that earned a real-Postgres test: 'one deposit and one rental fee per rental' is enforced by two partial UNIQUE indexes (migration 1754900000000), and `payments-collection.e2e-spec.ts` provokes them three ways — a second call, TWO CONCURRENT calls that both read an empty ledger ([200, 422] with exactly one row), and a raw INSERT that bypasses the app entirely. The race is translated at the adapter edge into `CollectionConflictError`, then answered with the SAME outcome as the pre-check plus the amount now on file (ADR 0001 §2, the create-rental pattern). AC3: a returned or cancelled rental answers `rejected_rental_closed` + currentStatus and writes nothing. AC4: an empty call is `rejected_nothing_to_record` — a business outcome, since each field is valid alone and only the use case is wrong — while a 0₫ amount stays a 400 envelope. AC5 (vitest + Playwright): the return dialog now reads the ledger and refunds `deposit collected − suggested late fee`; with no deposit on file it falls back to the catalog and SAYS so instead of presenting a reference figure as money the shop holds. Read side gained `summary` (per-kind totals, computed in the projection so two screens spend one number) and `RentalDressDto.agreedPrice` from `rental_items.price`. Gates: be 114 unit · 46 e2e · fe 83 vitest · qr-admin 17 · contract:check, check, lint, arch, both builds green (BE + contract + both clients land in one commit) · `pnpm --filter fe e2e` green against the real stack, exercising record-then-refund end to end. Then reviewed by codex CLI on the PR, which found four further money defects — each fixed with a test that fails without the fix: (1) recording money re-checks the rental status under a row lock INSIDE the write transaction, because the service pre-check alone let a concurrent return close the rental between check and insert; (2) a ledger read that FAILED, and later one still in flight, both read as no-deposit-collected on the two money screens, so a refund could be offered for money the shop never took — an unknown basis now blocks and says so; (3) the settlement sends the basis it computed from and the return write verifies it under the same rental row lock, refusing with rejected_deposit_basis_changed and writing nothing, which is the only place that check cannot be raced past; (4) a 0 typed into one collect field made the API reject the whole request under @Min(1), losing the other, valid amount with it.
acceptance: AC1: staff record the deposit and/or the rental fee of an open rental in one action; the ledger shows exactly the amounts entered, with the note on every row
AC2: a second recording of the same kind is refused and states the amount already on file — including when two devices submit at the same time
AC3: a returned or cancelled rental refuses money with its current status
AC4: calling the action with nothing to record is refused as a business outcome, not a 500
AC5: the return dialog computes the refund from the deposit ACTUALLY collected, and says so when no deposit was ever recorded

features.title: Owner creates/locks/reset-passwords staff accounts; login moves to username/password (FR-AUTH-04 + FR-AUTH-01 change)
features.evidence: 2026-08-10: spec approved same day (owner accepted all §6 recommendations verbatim), then implemented and re-synced as-built (§7). Migration 1755000000000: username UNIQUE lower() backfilled from the email local-part, active flag, email column DROPPED — one identity column is one truth. AC1: Username VO (lowercase, 3-30 [a-z0-9._-]) + pre-check + UsernameConflictError translated at the repository so the race answers the same rejected_username_taken with the normalized name — proven by unit and by e2e three ways (different casing, two concurrent creates yielding exactly one row, raw INSERT). AC2: login answers rejected_account_locked ONLY after the password matched (lock state is unprobeable — wrong password stays generic, proven in the same e2e); refresh reads active in the user-loading query and dies generically; reactivation restores login; live access tokens ride out their TTL (stated trade-off). AC3: no DELETE /users/* exists — lock only, FKs stay safe. AC4: user:manage (owner-only, fail-closed) guards all four commands + the list; staff calling any of them gets the GENERIC.FORBIDDEN envelope, proven over HTTP. AC5: reset-password kills the old password and works on locked accounts (it prepares the unlock). Extra rules: the owner cannot deactivate self (checked before the row is even loaded), the list never carries a hash (key-level e2e), GET /users is unpaginated by design (<10 rows). FE: /users route self-guards on me.role (display; BE policy is the rule), table with per-row lock/unlock through ConfirmDialog + reset-password dialog + create dialog putting rejected_username_taken on the field; login forms of BOTH clients moved to username; nav link owner-only. Everything that signs in changed in the same commit: seed (SEED_OWNER_USERNAME=owner), smoke.sh, Playwright happy path, e2e harness, MSW fixtures, CI env. Gates: be 126 unit (+12) / 55 e2e (+9, 13-case identity-users.e2e-spec.ts) on real Postgres, fe 87 vitest (+4 users cases incl. staff-redirect and confirm-dialog lock), qr-admin 17, fe+qr-admin builds green, lint green, contract re-emitted and both clients regenerated in this commit. Found while testing: the local .env carried LATE_FEE_PER_DRESS_PER_DAY=20000 (one zero short of the approved rate) — fixed locally; .env.example was already correct.
acceptance: AC1: a created account signs in with its username/password; duplicate usernames (case-insensitive) are refused, race included
AC2: a locked account can neither log in nor refresh; reactivation restores it; live access tokens die only by TTL (stated trade-off)
AC3: the contract has no user delete
AC4: staff calling any user-management endpoint gets the fail-closed 403 envelope
AC5: after reset-password the old password is dead and the new one works
